scenes.heading: buttons that forget
scenes.narration: What if buttons forgot you after every click? This tiny kit redraws windows each frame for you, skipping hand-placed pixels. Picture a short-order kitchen tracking one press.

scenes.heading: the front counter
scenes.narration: You press keys as the app user, and you click too. The demo app, your per-frame loop helper, loops frames so you see change.

scenes.heading: the forgetful kitchen
scenes.narration: The ui core, microui, a tiny C library, rebuilds widgets, clickable buttons, from scratch for you. It records the command list, simple kitchen tickets, so drawing stays trivial.

scenes.heading: the ticket window
scenes.narration: Behind tickets the sdl renderer, an SDL drawing helper, paints for you. It presents the frame, or you see nothing.

scenes.heading: follow one press
scenes.narration: To trail one press, you press keys on the OK button for action. The demo app declares widgets for the open window for you. Next the ui core records commands into the command list as rect, a colored box, plus text. Then the sdl renderer reads commands from tickets. It shows the frame with OK lit for you.

scenes.heading: the whole trip
scenes.narration: Across the whole trip you, as the app user, tap through the demo app, the ui core, the command list, and the sdl renderer back to a lit button. So forgetting each frame keeps the kit tiny, yet familiar for you.
